title: Intent to Destroy
description: Bill C-7 knowingly removed the reasonably foreseeable natural death safeguard, expanding state-administered death to the disabled and vulnerable. Parliament was warned of this outcome. The explicit intent to broaden the cohort sits on the Hansard record under Article 6(a).
evidence: Primary Source: Statutes of Canada 2021 (Bill C-7) • Track 2 Volume: 776 Canadians in 2024.

title: The Killing Fields
description: Track 2 deaths documented by Ontario's Chief Coroner confirm the non-terminal cohort. Vulnerable Canadians are being processed through the system while facing compounding pressures of poverty, housing deprivation, and clinical isolation.
evidence: Evidence: Ontario MDRC Reports • Scope: ~4.7% of total 2024 MAID volume.

title: Bodily and Mental Harm
description: State agencies repeatedly offered MAID to citizens seeking treatment. Veterans Affairs agents proactively suggested death over care, while patients were offered MAID while being denied necessary home support.
evidence: Article 6(b): Causing serious harm • Palliative Access: <30% receive needed care.

title: Conditions Calculated to Destroy
description: Track 2 applicants face severe material deprivation before death. They fall into the lowest material-resources (28.4%) and highest residential-instability (48.3%) quintiles, demonstrating death where care and housing should be provided.
evidence: Demographics: 61% female (Ontario Track 2) • Article 6(c): Inflicting destructive conditions.

title: Coercion of the Vulnerable
description: With over 76,000 total MAID provisions, the system has become a default relief valve for a collapsing social safety net. When the only door the state opens without friction ends your life — that is structural coercion.
evidence: Impact: 5.1% of all Canadian deaths in 2024 • Result: Policy-driven extermination.
